method: Built-in imagegen; one substrate atlas; mechanical crop and pigment reduction only
prompt: Use case: game native pixelart. Create ONE four-state substrate sprite atlas for GenVo, top-down evolutionary survival game. Four clearly separated equal square cells in one horizontal row, transparent background and generous gutters. Each sprite is same-scale irregular ground patch intended for 32x32 native pixels, occupies about26x26 centered. Camera EXACT VERTICAL OVERHEAD looking straight DOWN at horizontal ground, no horizon or front surfaces. Cell1 wet reed-bed ROOT MAT: damp muted olive-brown mud with interlaced fine tan root/rhizome strands and a few flattened BROKEN dry strap-leaf fragments lying on ground. Cell2 thicket ROOT AND LEAF LITTER: asymmetrical thin woody roots crossing dark soil with scattered dead curled brown leaf fragments, low quiet contrast. Cell3 decomposer HOLLOW FLOOR: dark damp decomposing litter, irregular decayed wood fibers, shallow soil cavities and tiny pale fibrous streaks. Cell4 worn clearing floor: dry packed olive earth, exposed fine roots, shallow irregular wear marks and a few restrained small grey pebbles. All four palettes cohesive with earthy muted green terrain: deep #263b2b, muted #46533a, soil #675d3e, subdued ochre #8b8053, soft #a09770, rare #b3aa84. Pixel clusters deliberate bold native low resolution enlarged nearest-neighbor, not noisy grain or soft photo. Each ground patch has irregular broken feathered-by-pixel silhouette and open transparent gaps, no solid square frame, no heavy black outline or cast shadow. Ground details richly organic yet quiet so a teal creature above remains readable. NO living plants, upright stems, reeds, canopy, grass blades standing up, flowers, berries, fruit, pods, mushrooms/caps, seeds, eggs, creatures, UI, text, labels, buildings, roots rising vertically, terrain walls, elevation, cliffs or isometric perspective. Substrates only, not food/interactable icons; each cell distinct horizontal ground texture, keep transparent space around and between cells.
